question: An 85-year-old man with a peripheral venous catheter who, one week after being hospitalized due to a stroke, begins with shivering and fever. Blood cultures are performed and from microbiology it is reported that gram positive cocci are growing in clusters. Pending the antibiogram, what is the most appropriate antibiotic treatment?
analysis: Given the presentation of shivering and fever in an elderly patient with gram positive cocci growing in clusters from blood cultures, the most appropriate initial antibiotic choice would be to cover for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) infection, which is commonly seen in healthcare settings. Vancomycin is the preferred choice for empiric treatment of suspected MRSA infections.
